messages:
Anya (PM): quick sync  sales surfaced a request for a paid high-throughput/priority add-on for ecommerce customers. want to align on packaging, launch gates, and contract constraints.
Maria (Product Finance): paste the sketch + expected uplift pls. need to model unit economics.
Anya (PM): naming draft: 'priority-throughput' add-on. packaging ideas: three capacity bands (10k, 50k, 200k req/day), soft-limit with throttled burst. monetization: percent uplift on requests or dedicated monthly fee. expectation: pilot customers ~20-30% rev uplift if priced competitively.
Sam (Sales): ACME (pilot) needs sustained 1k rps, p95 <250ms. they'll pay for predictability but need clear overage terms and rollback safety.
Kevin (Legal): constraints: no open-ended SLA liability in pilot. require overage cap, clear crediting workflow, and audit logs. include termination/rollback carveout if we need to evict reserved capacity.
Jasper (Eng): implementation questions: guarantee 1k rps via dedicated pools or priority scheduling? dedicated pools = predictable but costly; priority queues on shared pools = cheaper but riskier. also need autoscaler tweaks and eviction policy.
Anya (PM): initial plan: hybrid approach. top tier = reserved backends (dedicated lane). mid-tier = priority scheduling on shared pool with background preemption. fallback route: automatic downgrade to best-effort model variant on capacity stress.
Maria (Product Finance): pricing options: (A) fixed monthly + uplift, (B) percent surcharge per-priority request, (C) commitment tiers with credit-on-miss. which ops model fits best?
Jasper (Eng): prefer (C) for planning; credits are simpler than dynamic throttling. also easier to explain to infra.
Sam (Sales): enterprise buyers like fixed monthly (A). self-serve/midsize prefer (B). recommend we support both with clear mapping rules.
Kevin (Legal): contract asks: define 'priority request' (route tag), soft/hard caps, overage pricing at 1.5x standard, fallback behavior during incidents, 30-day notice for capacity changes. need standard template.
Anya (PM): proposed launch criteria (draft):
- Product: route tagging UI, opt-in per-route, console toggle for priority lanes.
- Infra: reserved pool implementation for top tier, priority scheduling for mid-tier, canary routing.
- Observability: per-request priority label, token/cost breakdown, SLA monitoring with alerts for >5% breach in 1h.
- Billing: invoice lines for add-on, overage calc, test crediting flow.
- Legal: template with overage & rollback clauses.
- Pilot: 3 customers (1 enterprise, 2 midsize) for 6 weeks; success if avg p95 meets targets and cost within 10% of forecast.
Maria (Product Finance): I'll build unit-econ model with 30/50/80% utilization scenarios.
Jasper (Eng): infra tasks: autoscaler policy updates, eviction policy, prefix caching behavior under priority, end-to-end load tests. estimate 4 sprints for pilot-ready infra.
Sam (Sales): timeline: start now -> Q3 pilot cohort (ACME + 2). need collateral and a simple price sheet.
Anya (PM): decision items: (1) support dual-pricing (A+B) vs commitment-only (C), (2) require dedicated capacity for top tier or allow priority-scheduling, (3) pilot gating metrics. votes?
Maria (Product Finance): vote: (C) commitment-first; allow (A) as negotiated enterprise add-on.
Sam (Sales): vote: dual-pricing; enterprise = A, midsize = B, discount C for commitments.
Kevin (Legal): vote: require dedicated for top tier. legal will draft contract snippet once product provides language.
Jasper (Eng): vote: require dedicated for top tier to meet latency SLAs.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: note: priority-lane canary load test scheduled 2024-09-10T20:00Z (job #5543).
Anya (PM): next steps: Maria -> unit-econ; Jasper -> infra runbook + estimates; Kevin -> contract snippet; Sam -> secure pilot customers. I'll consolidate spec and post updated doc by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
